principles.statement: Prefers strong brand presence with the logo as a clear anchor, not a tiny corner mark
evidence: The boss enlarged the logo on the landing page hero and explained brand recognition matters more than whitespace here

principles.statement: Prefers calm, spacious layouts over dense ones — whitespace is a feature, not wasted area
evidence: The boss removed three decorative blocks from the homepage and said the page was fighting itself

principles.statement: Prefers direct, concrete copy over vague startup language like 'unlock', 'empower', 'transform'
evidence: The boss rewrote a hero headline three times to remove jargon and explained the user already knows what we do

principles.statement: Prefers a single high-contrast CTA per screen — competing buttons split attention
evidence: The boss demoted secondary buttons to text links to make the primary action obvious

principles.statement: Avoids decorative gradients and shadows unless they serve a functional purpose
evidence: The boss flattened a hero gradient and said it was a relic from 2014

principles.statement: Prefers explicit readability over premature abstraction — a few extra lines beats a clever helper
evidence: The boss inlined a tiny utility function during review and said the abstraction was hiding what was actually happening
